alternatives: Lacosamide is a non-enzyme-inducing alternative if levetiracetam is not tolerated
contraindications: Enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital) increase dexamethasone clearance and interact with chemotherapy; avoid when a non-inducing agent is suitable.
interactions: Dexamethasone and metformin or sitagliptin: corticosteroids antagonize glucose-lowering therapy; dose-related hyperglycemia, often needing insulin while on steroids.
Dexamethasone and aspirin: additive risk of gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding; consider gastric protection.
Dexamethasone and atorvastatin or amlodipine: dexamethasone is a weak CYP3A4 inducer; no clinically significant change expected.
Levetiracetam with metformin, sitagliptin, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin or dexamethasone: no clinically significant interaction (renally cleared, no CYP involvement).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right temporal mass of 5.4 x 4.8 x 4.6 cm with thick irregular peripheral rim and nodular enhancement, central necrosis, internal hemorrhagic foci, mild rim restriction, extensive vasogenic edema along the optic radiation and 4 mm leftward midline shift
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, SWI, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right temporal lobe mass, internal hemorrhagic foci, degree of edema, and proximity to eloquent structures
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI with susceptibility imaging characterizes the mass and its hemorrhage, defines the mass effect and its relation to eloquent structures, and plans the approach; it precedes any tissue sampling (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: rCBV 4.6 at the enhancing rim and 2.1 in the peritumoral zone support a high-grade neoplasm and target the sampling

action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion supports a high-grade neoplasm (rCBV above 1.75) and identifies the most vascular region to sample; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA 10.3 with lipid-lactate at the rim and raised peritumoral choline (Cho/Cr 2.6) support an infiltrative high-grade neoplasm
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) of the enhancing rim and the peritumoral zone to characterize the metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: Raised choline beyond the enhancing margin supports an infiltrative glioma over a metastasis; spectroscopy supports, tissue decides.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right temporal focal slowing with occasional right anterior to mid temporal sharp waves; no electrographic seizure recorded
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG to characterize the three stereotyped staring spells with lip-smacking
action_criteria.rationale: Stereotyped staring with lip-smacking is probable focal impaired-awareness seizure semiology; EEG characterizes the spells, and antiseizure treatment does not wait for it (AIOM supportive care).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary malignancy identified; no pulmonary, hepatic, or osseous metastatic disease; supports primary brain tumor as the working diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Order CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast as staging to exclude an extracranial primary malignancy, particularly given the hemorrhagic tumor appearance
action_criteria.rationale: Optional: a hemorrhagic solitary metastasis is on the imaging differential and he is a former smoker, but tissue is diagnostic.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Platelets 118 x10^9/L (mild thrombocytopenia, above the usual neurosurgical threshold), glucose 164 mg/dL with HbA1c 8.1%, normal coagulation: no contraindication to surgery once the platelet count is confirmed
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory workup: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), and type & screen in anticipation of surgical craniotomy
action_criteria.rationale: Platelets, coagulation, electrolytes, glucose and type and screen must be known before a neurosurgical procedure and before dexamethasone.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: KPS 80, ECOG 1: normal activity with effort and mild left hemiparesis
action_criteria.label: Score the current performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: Treatment selection after the integrated diagnosis depends on performance status; KPS below 70 is the unfavourable threshold (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left-hemisphere language dominance (laterality index 0.86); right face motor area 5 mm and hand motor area 12 mm from the tumor margin
action_criteria.label: Order functional MRI to lateralize language and map the right face and hand motor areas before resection
action_criteria.rationale: The tumor extends to within 5 mm of the inferior precentral gyrus, and language dominance must be confirmed before a temporal resection; functional MRI plans the extent of a maximal safe resection (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right optic radiation (Meyer's loop) displaced and thinned in contact with the tumor; right corticospinal tract displaced medially, 6 mm away, fibers preserved
action_criteria.label: Order DTI tractography of the right optic radiation and corticospinal tract before resection
action_criteria.rationale: Edema and tumor involve the optic radiation and the corticospinal tract is displaced; tractography plans the resection margins (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 (gliosarcoma subtype) with IDH1 R132H negative, ATRX retained and MGMT promoter unmethylated
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by maximal safe resection of the right temporal lesion, or stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, ATRX and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery is the first option for a resectable glioma and should be as extensive as safely possible (AIOM; EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis and the molecular results that select treatment; gliosarcoma is a histological subtype of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype (WHO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Dexamethasone will worsen glycemic control on metformin and sitagliptin and insulin is likely to be needed; aspirin is stopped about 7 days before craniotomy; levetiracetam has no relevant interaction
action_criteria.label: Check interactions of levetiracetam and dexamethasone with the current metformin, sitagliptin, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin, with attention to glycemic control and perioperative bleeding
action_criteria.rationale: Recommended: there is a concrete pharmacodynamic interaction (dexamethasone against oral glucose-lowering drugs in a diabetic with HbA1c 8.1%) and an antiplatelet drug before neurosurgery.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture: the 4 mm midline shift and mass effect create herniation risk
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide) before tissue diagnosis and WHO 2021-integrated molecular profiling are established
Do not prescribe enzyme-inducing antiepileptic drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital): they lower dexamethasone and chemotherapy exposure
Do not stop dexamethasone abruptly once started; taper gradually to avoid rebound edema and adrenal insufficiency
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the right temporal lesion, with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography and intraoperative mapping, with stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5).

Treat the stereotyped staring spells with lip-smacking as probable focal impaired-awareness seizures: obtain an EEG to characterise them and start levetiracetam; avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs.

Start dexamethasone for symptomatic vasogenic oedema (for example 4 mg every 6 to 8 hours after a loading dose when mass effect is marked) at the lowest effective dose, with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery; with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c 8.1%, expect to add insulin while on dexamethasone.
Confirm the platelet count of 118 x10^9/L with a repeat count and blood film before surgery, and stop aspirin (primary prevention) about 7 days before craniotomy.
Advise no driving because of the seizures and the left upper quadrantanopia, in line with local licensing rules.

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, at age 70 or under with KPS 70 or more, radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp 2005; EANO 2021).

metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty: The internal hemorrhagic foci and imaging heterogeneity introduce a hemorrhagic metastasis as a serious alternative differential requiring active exclusion with staging CT and advanced MRI. Three embedded red herrings (mild thrombocytopenia, elevated inflammatory markers, diabetic immunosuppression) create plausible but spurious pressure toward hematologic or infectious diagnoses. Correct identification of gliosarcoma requires integration of advanced MRI (perfusion + spectroscopy + functional/DTI) with histopathology showing the defining biphasic pattern.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Three required actions (contrast MRI, pre-operative labs, tissue by resection or biopsy) and seven recommended (perfusion, spectroscopy, EEG, performance status, functional MRI, DTI, drug check); three red herrings; the hemorrhagic appearance widens the imaging differential and the gliosarcoma subtype is seen only on histology

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Khalid Al-Rashidi is a 57-year-old right-handed civil engineer who presents to the inpatient neurology service with a six-week history of progressive headaches, word-finding difficulty, and a visual field problem that his wife first noticed while they were driving. He reports that the headaches began insidiously approximately six weeks ago as a dull, pressure-like sensation localized predominantly to the right temporal and parietal region. Initially, he attributed them to work-related stress and inadequate sleep. Over the subsequent two weeks, the headaches became more persistent, occurring daily, and were notably worse upon awakening in the morning. Acetaminophen provided minimal relief. He began avoiding bright light and found himself retreating to quiet, darkened rooms, which he attributed to what he assumed was a migraine variant — he had no prior history of migraine. Approximately four weeks ago, his wife noticed that he was struggling to find words during dinner conversations, occasionally substituting descriptive phrases for objects he should have easily named. He acknowledged this difficulty but minimized it, attributing it to fatigue. Two weeks ago, she observed that he repeatedly failed to notice a car approaching from the left upper side while seated in the passenger seat, and he subsequently stopped driving out of caution. He has experienced three episodes in the past month that he describes as brief 'freezing' spells lasting ten to fifteen seconds, during which he stares blankly and is unresponsive; his wife noticed slight lip-smacking during one of these episodes. He did not seek medical attention immediately after these events, attributing the first to exhaustion and the second to hypoglycemia given his diabetes. At his primary care follow-up one week ago, brief cognitive testing revealed anomic errors, and his physician identified the left visual field deficit on confrontation testing. A non-contrast head CT the same day showed a right temporal mass with surrounding hypodensity and 4 mm leftward midline shift. He was admitted for urgent neurological evaluation. He denies frank hemiplegia, dysarthria, dysphagia, nausea, vomiting, or unintentional weight loss. He has not had fever, chills, or recent infections. He has no known history of malignancy or immunosuppression. He was born and raised in Jordan and emigrated to the United States 22 years ago.
